summary: Stop --agent/--compact from stripping a blocked key (comments) when it is the response's only payload array; resolve the verbose-object blocklist per response instead of applying it unconditionally.
reason: compactVerboseObjectFields lists 'comments' as a verbose sidecar, but on the comments commands that key IS the payload. Stripping it returned {"success":true,"cursor":"..."} with exit 0 and no data on every comments-shaped command across six platforms - a credit spent per call, nothing returned. Durable rule for reprints: never strip the only array in a single-object response, where 'array' for competitor-counting means a compactObjectArrayValue-shaped payload (non-empty array of objects), so scalar or empty sidecar arrays cannot re-trigger the loss.
validated_outcome: Live verification with --agent on all six comments commands (instagram, tiktok, youtube, facebook, reddit, rumble): 0 comments before, 10-25 after, envelope fields intact; empty-comments responses return comments: [] rather than dropping the key. Unit tests pin payload-kept, empty-array-kept, scalar-array-competitor, empty-sidecar-competitor, sidecar-stripped, and description-stripped cases.
